It checked that two credentials Stratos minted for one space had different ids and each read the member's record from the October PDS through com.atproto.space.listRecords. Stratos depends on a host accepting a Stratos credential: the named journey carries that half, and two of the surviving suites carry the journey in a ported form. The different ids existed only so that the probe could revoke one; at the November reference the revocation method is renamed com.atproto.space.notifyCredentialsRevoked, and Stratos never sends it, so that half has nothing to port to.

It checked that a revocation notice with an issuer other than the space authority was refused with 403 and left the credential readable. The October probe signed com.atproto.space.notifyCredentialRevoked with the Stratos service key, sent it to the October PDS, and read back with com.atproto.space.listRecords. At the November reference the method is renamed com.atproto.space.notifyCredentialsRevoked; the PDS serves it and takes it only from the space authority. Stratos answers it as an unknown method and never sends it: a credential Stratos mints lapses at its expiry, and Stratos depends on no host revocation. The probe tested how a host handles a notice Stratos never sends, so it is superseded, nothing to port to.

carriedBy.title: answers them as unknown whoever asks
carriedBy.proves: Each upstream writer-set and revocation route gets 501 when the request carries a bearer authorization header.

carriedBy.title: notices a handler registered for one of the routes
carriedBy.proves: With a listWriters handler placed before the service router, the unknown-method check fails and names that route.

entries.reason: The in-process service test answers the upstream writer routes, under their November names listWriters and notifyRepoUpdate where the October probe sent listRepos and notifyWrite, as unknown methods; the October probe needed a PDS that speaks them.

carriedBy.title: a_member_removed_during_the_poll_promotes_nothing
carriedBy.proves: A member removed while their poll waits on a page ends the cycle as Retry, and none of that member's posts is served.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust test (a member removed during a poll promotes nothing); the October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_generation_bumped_between_the_read_and_the_promotion_is_unauthorized
carriedBy.proves: A promotion whose member generation was reset after the target was read is refused as unauthorized and writes no record or post.

carriedBy.title: a_member_who_left_cannot_be_promoted
carriedBy.proves: A promotion for a member removed after the target was read is refused as unauthorized.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust tests. A November poll verifies and promotes the commit of its last page, so a removal during that last read is a removal before the promotion write, and the store refuses that write after a generation reset and after a removal; the October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_departed_member_loses_the_verified_state_and_the_other_member_keeps_it
carriedBy.proves: Removing one of two promoted members deletes that member's verified state and stored paths and leaves the other member's.

carriedBy.title: a_member_who_left_cannot_be_replaced
carriedBy.proves: After one member is removed, the other member's post, boundary, interaction and verified-state rows are unchanged, and a replacement for the removed member is refused.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust tests (a departed member's rows go and another member's stay). The other member of the October driver held Stratos custody; the named tests keep another PDS-custody member, and the journey runs the mixed case against a host. The October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_stale_generation_changes_nothing
carriedBy.proves: After a member is removed and added again, a replacement under the old generation is refused as unauthorized and changes no row.

carriedBy.title: reading_the_base_under_a_stale_generation_is_refused
carriedBy.proves: Reading a member's base with a generation other than the current one is refused as unauthorized.

carriedBy.title: a_member_re_enrolled_with_a_new_generation_starts_with_a_replacement
carriedBy.proves: A member removed and added again while a poll waits ends that poll as Retry, and a cycle holding the old generation is turned away at its first base read.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust tests (the generation is checked at each store write and at each base read). The October run also waited for a logged target failure; a stale cycle now ends as Retry, which is not a failure. The October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_member_re_enrolled_with_a_new_generation_starts_with_a_replacement
carriedBy.proves: After the stale cycle is refused, the next cycle replaces the member's state under a new generation and its digest equals the host's.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust tests (a member added again starts with a replacement under a new generation); the October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_member_who_left_stays_gone_and_cannot_be_replaced_after_the_store_reopens
carriedBy.proves: A member removed from a file store has no generation, base or rows after the store is closed and reopened, the other member's rows are unchanged, and a replacement for the removed member is refused.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust test, which closes and reopens a real encrypted file store after the removal, where the October driver restarted the feed generator; the October driver held pages and detected a terminal page by a body commit and waited for a log word that no longer exists, so it cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: pages_of_one_cycle_draw_on_the_same_budget
carriedBy.proves: One value budget charged by three equal pages refuses the third once two have used it, and its used count does not reset between pages.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust test. The October budget accumulated over passes because staged pages carried from one pass to the next; a November cycle carries nothing into the next, so the budget a split read cannot evade is the one every page of a cycle draws on. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion about stage accounting cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: creates_updates_and_deletes_over_one_two_and_three_pages_promote
carriedBy.proves: A poll that updates one post, deletes another and creates three, over one, two or three pages, serves exactly one URI for each remaining path and none for the deleted one, and its digest equals the host state.

carriedBy.title: a_replacement_leaves_unchanged_rows_as_they_were_and_rewrites_the_changed_one
carriedBy.proves: A whole-repo replacement that edits one of three posts rewrites that post row with the new timestamps and leaves the other two rows as they were.

carriedBy.title: a_delete_removes_the_post_and_the_interactions_that_pointed_at_it
carriedBy.proves: A promoted delete removes the served post and the like that pointed at it, and only the like keeps a path row.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust tests. The October run required a same-path replacement and a delete each to leave one published row or none, and the published byte total to move by exactly the size change of that row. The named tests cover the rows: one row per path after an update, the changed row rewritten, the deleted post gone. Not covered: the published byte total after a same-path update or a delete; no test reads it. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_page_past_the_decoded_value_budget_fails_and_one_at_it_is_accepted
carriedBy.proves: A poll whose page decodes one value past the budget fails as RepoOverBudget and changes no table, and one at the budget is promoted.

carriedBy.title: an_archive_over_a_limit_fails_as_over_budget_and_changes_nothing
carriedBy.proves: A whole-repo archive with more records or bytes than allowed fails the cycle as RepoOverBudget and leaves every table as it was.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust test of the budget, deadline or interruption it exercised; staging no longer exists, so the October assertion about stage accounting cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: an_empty_database_reaches_version_eleven_without_the_stage_tables
carriedBy.proves: A new database at the latest migration has none of the stage tables and no rows of verified space state.

carriedBy.title: a_version_ten_database_with_rows_in_the_five_tables_reaches_eleven_and_loses_only_them
carriedBy.proves: Migrating a database that holds rows in the stage tables drops those tables and leaves every other row as it was.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust tests. The October run required a promotion to empty every stage table and leave published bytes equal to the promoted value only. The stage tables no longer exist, as the named migration tests show, so a promotion has no staged accounting to release. Not covered: the published byte total after a promotion; no test reads it. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_pass_over_every_kind_of_outcome_counts_each_and_logs_one_reason_line
carriedBy.proves: In one pass where three targets fail, one of them on a first RepoNotFound answer that clears nothing, another target still promotes and the pass counts each outcome.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust test: failing targets leave another target of the same pass to promote. Its failures are host refusals, not a budget overrun, which is what failed in the October run. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion about stage accounting cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_promotion_and_a_replacement_over_the_projection_maximum_are_refused_and_change_nothing
carriedBy.proves: With the projection maximum one byte above what is published, a one-post promotion and a replacement for the same member are each refused as over budget and change none of the member's rows, and both succeed once the maximum is raised.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust test. The October limit was a configured cap on staged bytes across targets (FEEDGEN_STAGE_GLOBAL_MAX_BYTES), refused when two targets together passed it while each stayed under its own byte cap. The present limit is the configured projection maximum (FEEDGEN_PROJECTION_MAX_BYTES): a write is refused when the bytes it adds and everything already published pass it. The limit is store-wide, but the named test has one member only. Not covered: a refusal caused by what other members or Stratos-custody posts have published, and any per-member byte cap, which no longer exists. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_promotion_and_a_replacement_over_the_projection_maximum_are_refused_and_change_nothing
carriedBy.proves: With the projection maximum one byte above what is published, a one-post promotion and a replacement for the same member are each refused as over budget and change none of the member's rows, and both succeed once the maximum is raised.

carriedBy.title: the_bytes_a_write_adds_are_the_length_of_each_field_of_its_rows
carriedBy.proves: The byte count the projection maximum charges for a row is the length of each of its fields; for the four rows of two creates, a like and a delete it is pinned at 1,571.

carriedBy.title: published_bytes_counts_posts_and_interactions
carriedBy.proves: The published total that a write is checked against is the sum of the stored post and interaction bytes, and an interaction's stored bytes are the length of its text fields plus a fixed overhead.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust tests. The October run read the stored database after a refused page: no staged row or byte remained, published bytes were unchanged, and the published byte count equalled the measured size of each stored post. Nothing is staged now, and a refused write changes no row. The named tests pin how a write is charged and what it is checked against. Not covered: that the bytes recorded for a stored space post equal the length of its fields. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_promotion_past_the_per_member_record_limit_is_refused_whole
carriedBy.proves: With 20,000 verified records held for one member, a promotion that adds one more is refused as over budget and leaves the member's base and record count unchanged.

carriedBy.title: a_set_past_the_per_member_record_limit_is_refused_before_anything_is_hashed
carriedBy.proves: A whole-repo replacement of 20,001 records for one member, under a commit whose digest cannot match, is refused as over budget rather than as a digest mismatch, and changes neither member.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust tests. The October limit was a configured cap on the rows one target could stage (FEEDGEN_STAGE_TARGET_MAX_ROWS), refused while byte room remained. The present limit is a fixed number of verified records per member and space (MAX_SPACE_REPO_RECORDS, 20,000, in stratos-feedgen-ng/src/config.rs), checked when a promotion or a replacement is written. Not covered: a cap an operator can set. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_promotion_past_the_store_wide_row_limit_is_refused_whole
carriedBy.proves: With another member's verified state recording 499,990 records, a promotion that takes the member from 10 records to 11 is refused as over budget and changes none of the member's state, paths, served posts or interactions.

carriedBy.title: a_set_past_the_store_wide_row_limit_is_refused_whole
carriedBy.proves: With another member's verified state recording 499,997 records, a replacement that takes the member from three records to four is refused as over budget and leaves the member's rows unchanged.

entries.reason: Partly carried by the named Rust tests. The October limit was a configured cap on the rows staged across all targets (FEEDGEN_STAGE_GLOBAL_MAX_ROWS), refused when two targets together passed it while each stayed under its own cap. The present limit is a fixed number of verified records across every member of the store (MAX_SPACE_VERIFICATION_ROWS, 500,000), checked at the write. The named tests write the other member's record count straight into its verified state; no records are synced for it. Not covered: a configured cap, and two members that each sync real records up to the limit. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

Not covered today. The October run required a health answer within two seconds while sync was over its budget, and no current test makes a health or feed request while a sync cycle runs. The health handler reads the readiness gate and the scheduler status, not the store; a test would hold a store write open, request /health, and require an answer within that bound. Until one exists only the named journey of the prepared suite carries it.

carriedBy.title: a_promotion_that_never_commits_leaves_nothing_and_a_full_one_survives_reopening
carriedBy.proves: A promotion dropped before its commit leaves no base, record, post or interaction on a reopened file store, and a full promotion afterwards survives another reopen.

carriedBy.title: a_replacement_that_never_commits_leaves_the_earlier_state_and_a_full_one_survives_reopening
carriedBy.proves: A replacement dropped before its commit leaves the earlier verified rows on a reopened file store, and a full replacement afterwards survives another reopen.

entries.reason: The behaviour is inverted on purpose, and the named Rust tests pin the inverted behaviour, not the October one. The October feed generator kept the staged cursor of an interrupted pass to resume from; the November one stages nothing, so an interrupted cycle must leave nothing and the next cycle starts from the verified base. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.

carriedBy.title: a_crashed_poll_leaves_no_state_and_the_next_poll_starts_from_the_verified_rev
carriedBy.proves: A poll dropped while its second page is outstanding writes nothing, and the next poll asks from the verified revision with no cursor and promotes to the host state.

carriedBy.title: since_is_the_verified_revision_on_every_request_and_the_page_cursor_is_never_stored
carriedBy.proves: Every request of a poll sends the verified revision as since, and the next poll starts again from the new verified revision with no cursor.

entries.reason: Replaced by the named Rust tests. The October run let a stage pass its age limit, waited for the cleanup to remove the staged cursor, and required the next request to resume from the verified cursor. Nothing is stored between pages now, so there is nothing to expire, and every poll starts from the verified revision. The dropped poll in the first test runs in one process on one store; a dropped write on a reopened file store is the interrupted-stage entry. Staging no longer exists, so the October assertion cannot pass on any current build.
